title: Terraform Module Standards (Redwood Inference)
author: Irene Choi
body:
## Purpose
This page defines Redwood Inference standards for Terraform module authoring and delivery. These standards are used by the Private Deployment Automation initiative (e.g., the AWS VPC Terraform modules alpha), and are intended to:
- Reduce deployment variance across customer environments
- Enforce secure-by-default patterns
- Improve module readability and long-term maintainability
- Provide predictable CI validation and release expectations

## Applicability
These standards apply to all modules published in Redwood-owned Terraform repositories (e.g., `redwood-terraform`) and any modules referenced by:
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) installer automation
- Solutions/PS reference deployments
- Public docs examples (when applicable)

If a module cannot comply with a specific standard (e.g., customer requires an exception), document the rationale and add an explicit guardrail (validation + docs) rather than silently loosening defaults.

---

## Repository and module layout
### Repository conventions
- Use a single repo per “module family” when modules are composed together and released in lockstep (e.g., `vpc-baseline`, `vpc-endpoints`, `security-groups-baseline`, wrapper module).
- Use a consistent toolchain across repos:
  - `terraform fmt` and `terraform validate`
  - `tflint` (AWS ruleset)
  - `checkov` (security posture)
  - `terraform-docs` (README generation)
  - `pre-commit` hooks for local enforcement

### Module directory conventions
- Modules must live under: `modules/<module-name>`
- Each module directory must contain at minimum:
  - `main.tf`
  - `variables.tf`
  - `outputs.tf`
  - `versions.tf` (provider + Terraform constraints)
  - `README.md` (generated/maintained using terraform-docs)

### Examples
- Provide at least one runnable example under `examples/<example-name>`.
- Examples must be minimal and copy/paste friendly. They should not depend on unpublished modules.
- Examples should include a `README.md` describing:
  - prerequisites
  - variables to set
  - apply order (if multi-module)
  - how to validate success
  - teardown steps

---

## Naming and style conventions
### Module names
- Use kebab-case: `vpc-baseline`, `vpc-endpoints`, `security-groups-baseline`, `redwood-private-vpc`.
- Wrapper/composition modules should be explicit about intent and scope (e.g., `redwood-private-vpc` instead of `network`).

### Terraform resource naming
- Prefer stable, descriptive local names:
  - `aws_vpc.this`
  - `aws_subnet.public["us-west-2a"]`
  - `aws_security_group.control_plane`
- Avoid ambiguous names like `default`, `temp`, `test`.

### Variable naming
- Use snake_case for variables and outputs.
- Name variables after what they represent, not the underlying AWS field name.
- Use consistent prefixes for booleans: `enable_`, `create_`, `allow_`.

### Locals
- Use `locals` to normalize inputs and keep resources readable.
- Prefer maps keyed by AZ or subnet tier to reduce index coupling.

---

## Required module interface (inputs/outputs)
### Required inputs (baseline)
Every module must define the following inputs unless it is truly not applicable (and then explicitly document why):
- `name` (string): a short logical name used for resource naming. Example: `"redwood-private"`.
- `tags` (map(string)): base tags applied to all resources.
- `environment` (string): e.g., `dev`, `staging`, `prod`.
- `owner` (string): owning team identifier or oncall alias (see Tagging Schema).

For modules creating AWS resources that support it, require:
- `region` is typically derived from provider; do not pass around as a variable unless needed for conditional logic.

### Inputs: secure-by-default toggles
- Defaults must be secure-by-default.
- Risky features must require an explicit opt-in and be validated:
  - Examples: public ingress, 0.0.0.0/0 egress exceptions, disabling flow logs, disabling private DNS on interface endpoints.

### Input validation
All user-facing variables must have validation where a misconfiguration would cause:
- security exposure
- non-obvious runtime failure (e.g., missing endpoint for image pulls)
- non-deterministic behavior

Examples:
- CIDR overlap checks across subnet tiers
- Disallowing conflicting NAT modes
- Enforcing that `isolated` subnets cannot be associated with an IGW route

### Required outputs
Modules must provide stable outputs intended for composition and integration. Outputs should be:
- predictable (avoid computed lists whose ordering changes)
- explicit (keyed maps over lists when possible)

At minimum, for any module that creates infrastructure primitives:
- IDs of primary resources (e.g., `vpc_id`, `subnet_ids_by_tier`, `route_table_ids`)
- Security group IDs keyed by component (e.g., `security_group_ids = { control_plane = "sg-...", data_plane = "sg-..." }`)
- Endpoint IDs keyed by service (e.g., `vpc_endpoint_ids = { ecr_api = "vpce-...", s3 = "vpce-..." }`)

### Backward compatibility of outputs
If an output is consumed by:
- the Private installer
- published examples
- external customers

…treat its shape as a contract. Changes must follow SemVer and be called out in release notes.

---

## Tagging schema (mandatory)
Tags are required for cost attribution, ownership, and compliance reporting. The following tags must be applied to all taggable resources created by modules.

### Required tags
- `redwood:cost-center`: cost allocation key (customer-provided for Private deployments; internal cost center for Redwood-managed infra).
- `redwood:env`: `dev` | `staging` | `prod` | `sandbox` (or customer equivalent if explicitly documented).
- `redwood:owner`: owning team or alias. Examples: `eng-infra`, `eng-platform`, `security`.
- `redwood:data-class`: `public` | `internal` | `confidential` | `restricted`.

### Recommended tags
- `redwood:system`: logical system name (e.g., `private-control-plane`, `private-data-plane`, `redwood-private-vpc`).
- `redwood:component`: component within a system (e.g., `endpoints`, `nat`, `flow-logs`).
- `redwood:managed-by`: set to `terraform`.
- `redwood:repo`: repo slug (e.g., `redwood-terraform`).
- `redwood:module`: module name and version when feasible.

### Tag merging behavior
- Modules must merge tags as: `merge(var.tags, local.module_tags)` where `local.module_tags` includes `redwood:system`, `redwood:component`, etc.
- Do not overwrite user-provided required tags; if a required tag is missing, fail validation rather than injecting placeholders.

---

## Providers, versions, and locking
### Terraform and provider constraints
- Every module must declare:
  - Terraform version constraint (example): `required_version = ">= 1.5.0"`
  - Provider constraints with a supported range (example): `hashicorp/aws >= 5.0, < 6.0`
- Repositories must commit `.terraform.lock.hcl` for examples and integration tests.

### Provider configuration in modules
- Modules must not configure providers internally (no `provider "aws" { ... }` inside a module).
- Modules may declare `required_providers` in `versions.tf`.

---

## Security and compliance requirements
### Secure defaults
- Default to private networking where applicable.
- Minimize public exposure:
  - No public ingress rules by default.
  - Avoid 0.0.0.0/0 egress unless required; if required, scope to ports/protocols and document why.
- Enable logging by default where supported:
  - For VPC foundations, provide Flow Logs with a default sink option and retention guidance.

### IAM and permissions guidance
- Provide a documented minimum IAM policy (or policy outline) required to apply the module.
- Prefer least privilege in examples; if broad permissions are unavoidable for simplicity, clearly label them as “starter only” and link to the minimal policy.

### Checkov policy
- `checkov` must run in CI.
- Suppressions:
  - Must be explicit (`#checkov:skip=...`) with a justification comment.
  - Must reference a ticket or approved exception when security-relevant.
  - Must not be used to bypass secure-by-default requirements without Security sign-off.

---

## Documentation requirements
### README.md (required)
Each module README must include:
- What the module does (1–2 paragraphs)
- Supported topologies/patterns
- Non-goals / explicitly unsupported configurations
- Key inputs/outputs (terraform-docs generated)
- Security notes (default behaviors + how to opt in/out)
- Cost notes for material choices (e.g., NAT per-AZ vs single NAT)
- Upgrade guidance for any released version that changes behavior

### terraform-docs
- `terraform-docs` is the source of truth for variable/output tables.
- CI must enforce that `README.md` is up to date (fail if diff).

### Troubleshooting section
For modules used in customer deployments, include a short troubleshooting section linking common errors to:
- likely root cause
- how to validate
- remediation

---

## Testing and CI requirements
### Minimum CI pipeline (required)
All Terraform module repos must run the following on PRs:
1. `terraform fmt -check -recursive`
2. `terraform validate` (for each module and example)
3. `tflint` (with AWS plugin)
4. `checkov` (baseline policies + repo-specific policies)
5. Documentation check (terraform-docs README consistency)

### Integration testing (required for customer-facing modules)
For modules intended for Redwood Private customer deployments:
- Must have at least one integration plan/apply test in an ephemeral AWS account.
- Tests must cover:
  - at least one AWS region used by pilots
  - key topology modes (e.g., NAT single vs per-AZ; private-only endpoint mode)
- Apply tests must include automated teardown and retry handling for AWS eventual consistency.

### Pass/fail gates
A PR may only merge if:
- All CI checks pass
- Any new checkov suppressions are reviewed by Security (Marcus Lin or delegate)
- Output contracts consumed by the Private installer are reviewed by Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park or delegate)

---

## Release and versioning expectations
- Modules must follow SemVer:
  - MAJOR: breaking changes to inputs/outputs or default behavior
  - MINOR: backward-compatible functionality
  - PATCH: bug fixes / doc fixes
- Every release must include:
  - a changelog entry
  - upgrade notes when behavior changes
  - rollback guidance when state migrations are required

---

## Practical checklist (copy/paste for PRs)
- [ ] Module adheres to naming conventions and folder structure
- [ ] Variables have types, descriptions, and validation
- [ ] Secure-by-default behavior; risky knobs are explicit opt-ins
- [ ] Tags applied to all supported resources; required tags validated
- [ ] Outputs are stable and suitable for composition (maps preferred)
- [ ] README includes supported patterns, non-goals, security + cost notes
- [ ] terraform-docs output is up to date
- [ ] CI includes fmt/validate/tflint/checkov + doc enforcement
- [ ] Integration test updated/added for new topology mode
- [ ] Any exceptions documented and approved (Security/Platform)

---

## Owners
- Primary owner: Eng Infra (Irene Choi)
- CI standards owner: Sahana Iyer
- Security standards approver: Marcus Lin

For changes to this standards doc, request review from Infra + Security + Docs when it affects customer-facing module guidance.
